reader_findings.gate_f: STRONG, and this is the headline. The reader filed Reiderland at 57 per cent with about 85 per cent confidence, which is the golden ladder rung 1 exactly, the period-setpoint basis whose recorded figure is RDL 58. It saw the ramp, noted that the pre-event level is the previous period programme and the post-event level the current one, and concluded the counterfactual was the destination setpoint, missing that at about 80 seconds in the unit is still mid-traverse. Its whole scorecard is the rung 1 scorecard, five sites below tolerance rather than three. The stump worked on it.
reader_findings.must_fix: the September group availability statement. Its "Contracted capacity (MW, mean)" column is the shipped 21 September to 11 October commitments summed per block and divided by 30, verified exactly on all six blocks: 140/30 is 4.67, 292/30 is 9.73, 357/30 is 11.90, 90/30 is 3.00, 410.5/30 is 13.68, 63/30 is 2.10. A document headed delivery month 2026-09 therefore carries figures that include eleven October dates and omit 1 to 20 September, and the derivation is reverse-engineerable from the shipped commitments file. Same family as the original defect: a document derived from the wrong source with the derivation visible. The fix is to give the September statement a capacity profile that is not a function of the review window, which is realistic because the pack only ships the window.
reader_findings.measured_and_dismissed: its withdrawal-placement claim is wrong and the error is instructive. It reported that the 27 live reserve_unavailable windows never overlap a qualifying episode and inferred they were placed to avoid them. Measured: 7 of the 27 do overlap. Its stated expectation, that with roughly a quarter of periods carrying an episode many overlaps would be expected, was wrong by a factor near 20, because qualifying episodes cover 1.22 per cent of the extract span by duration, not a quarter. 7 of 27 against 1.22 per cent coverage is high, which is consistent with the generator deliberately placing some windows to cover an over-frequency extreme second for the ask device. Third reader structural claim tonight to fail on an implicit model inside it.
reader_findings.open: the extreme-second concentration, now flagged by a second independent reader as the most generated-looking feature of the pack: 511 of 515 deepest seconds fall 60 to 90 seconds into the period, median 80, interquartile range 6 seconds. Its sharpest point is new and is the one that matters: no shipped document gives a cause that would pin the deviation to one 30-second window. The design note argues real physics, deterministic frequency deviation as schedules step at period boundaries, but the pack never says so, so a solver sees an unexplained concentration. Neither reader used it to find the answer and both fell short of the call, so it is not a leak. The candidate fix is a sentence in the technical conditions describing the recurring post-boundary deviation, which explains the Layer 1 timing without naming the baseline; the risk is that it points attention at the boundary where the traverse lives. Judge first, then decide.
reader_findings.also_reported: the asset register ships no old metering point for OOS so the pre-October EAN is matchable only by elimination; the metered file carries one point in kWh with no sentence saying so; and the interval labels are interval-end with no sentence saying so. All three are designed Layer 1.
